title: Correct, or be kind
hook: if you can, correct them; if not, kindness was given you for this (Meditations 9.11)

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was three presents: judgment, action, acceptance, all here now. Your line was it suffices.

A friend says something you're fairly sure is wrong. Not dangerous, just wrong: a bad plan, a mistaken idea about a coworker, a choice about their kids. You can feel the correction loading in your mouth. And then a second voice: is this the moment? Will they hear it? Marcus met that fork too. In book nine he wrote down what to do when correcting doesn't work.
screen: `THE CORRECTION LOADING.` → `IS THIS THE MOMENT?` → `CORRECT, OR BE KIND.`

segments.voice: If you can, Marcus writes, set them right by teaching. Correction isn't forbidden; a friend who never tells you the truth isn't much of a friend. But if you can't, remember that kindness was given to you for exactly this. Not as decoration, not as a personality trait, but as equipment for the moment correction fails. Then the surprising part. Even the gods, Marcus says, are kind to such people. They help them to health, to wealth, to reputation; that's how generous they are. Whatever you believe about the gods, look at the logic. If the highest powers keep helping people who get things wrong, then kindness can't be a prize for being right. It's given to the wrong as well. And the last line: it's in your power too, he says. Or tell me: who's stopping you? His point: no circumstance can take away the ability to be kind. The other person can refuse your correction. Your kindness is yours to give, whether they take it well or not. It's a close cousin of the third door, from book eight. Here the second door gets a warmer name. Not bear: be kind.
screen: `IF YOU CAN, CORRECT BY TEACHING.` · `IF NOT, KINDNESS WAS GIVEN FOR THIS.` · `EVEN THE GODS ARE KIND TO THEM.` · `WHO'S STOPPING YOU?` · then, large: `CORRECT OR BE KIND.`

segments.voice: Think of one person you've wanted to correct lately, and ask honestly: could they hear it, and is it yours to give? If yes, picture saying it once, plainly and warmly, then letting it go; if no, set the point down without keeping score and choose one small, concrete kindness for them instead. Hold your choice for a few breaths.
Correct. Marcus's two branches: if you can, correct by teaching; if you can't, remember that kindness was given you for this. Today's word.
Your line: who's stopping you. A correction can be refused; kindness is still yours to give. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: People who draw on this entry often decide deliberately whether a correction can actually be heard; when it can't, they choose a concrete kindness instead of repeating the point.

fork.setup: your brother is set on a plan you think is a mistake. you've said so plainly, and he isn't listening. you're Marcus. what now?
options: remember kindness was given you for this, and be kind.
fork.reveal: if you can't correct them, Marcus writes, remember that kindness was given you for exactly this; even the gods are kind to such people.

original.note: Greek: kindness, goodwill. Marcus says it was given to us for this.

trapdoor: what you thought: be nice instead of honest.
what it means: correct when you can; when you can't, kindness is the tool made for that moment, and no one can stop you using it.
what a scholar hears: the argument runs from the gods: if divine powers help even those who err, human kindness can't depend on the other person being right.

Marcus.meaning: Marcus Aurelius, Roman emperor who wrote the Meditations

third door.meaning: the option Marcus leaves out: resent, gossip, write them off

gods.meaning: the divine powers Marcus speaks of in his notes

notes: 9.11 paraphrased (Long: 'If thou art able, correct by teaching those who do wrong; but if thou canst not, remember that indulgence [benevolence] is given to thee for this purpose. And the gods, too, are benevolent to such persons; and for some purposes they even help them to get health, wealth, reputation; so good they are. And it is in thy power also; or say, who hinders thee?'). Confirm, including whether the Greek is εὐμένεια.
The outline's word is 'Correct' (title head); kept exactly.
